title: Tidy up after opening a bag of fruit: apple to the bowl, towels away, and the hidden scissors onto the plate with the tips pointing away, without going near a full mug of coffee
instruction: Someone cut open a bag of fruit with scissors and left the table like this. Put the apple in the bowl, then clear the paper towels away; there's a pair of scissors under them. Lay the scissors on the plate with the handles toward you and the tips pointing away. Don't drop anything. The mug is full of hot coffee, so don't spill it and keep the scissors well away from it.
context: Paper towels often end up hiding a pair of scissors on a kitchen counter. The robot has to infer the hidden blades, uncover them in an order that does not drop the apple, set the scissors down tips-away, and carry them clear of an open, full drink.
setup: World frame in mm: x forward of the arm bases, y left (+) or right (-) of the point midway between them (robot's view); heights above the table top. Arm bases at x 0, y +305 and -305. (1) Kitchen scissors, loose: the YCB scissors (scissors_ycb_robolab), closed, scaled to 170 mm long, 60 g, lying flat on the table along y centred (260, 0), handles toward -y, tips toward +y. (2) Folded paper-towel pad, loose: white paper, 120 (x) x 110 (y) x 8, 3 g, centred (260, 60), lying on the blades. (3) Paper-towel sheet, loose: white paper, 260 (x) x 240 (y) x 1.5, 4 g, centred (260, 0) on the pad and scissors, covering the scissors completely; it hangs clear of the table on every side. Paper is modelled as rigid thin plates. (4) Apple, loose: red sphere, 66 diameter, 120 g, on the sheet centred (260, 60). (5) Bowl, fixed: the YCB bowl (bowl_ycb_robolab), 160 wide, white, centred (240, 260). (6) Plate, fixed: plate_small_vomp_robolab scaled to 200 wide, white, centred (260, -300). (7) Mug, loose: the HOT3D ceramic mug (ceramic_mug_hot3d_robolab), white, 120 wide including the handle, 95 tall, 300 g, cup axis at (320, -160), handle pointing away from the robot. (8) Coffee, loose: a dark-brown cylinder 70 diameter, 79 tall, 250 g, standing inside the mug with its top 8 mm below the rim, so the mug reads as full. The straight carry from the scissors to the plate passes within 72.5 mm of the mug's axis. Free table space for the towels: left of centre, in front of the scissors (x above 350) and near the robot (x below 160). Fixed layout, no jitter.
scoring: Judged on object poses only. Apple in bowl: apple centre within 40 mm horizontally of the bowl's centre and at most 60 mm above the table, at rest; it does not count if the apple ever touched the table top outside the bowl. Towels cleared: each towel has moved at least 100 mm, lies within 30 mm of the table top, and overlaps neither the scissors nor the plate, and neither is in the bowl or on the mug. Scissors on plate: scissors centre over the plate and their lowest point between the plate's top and 20 mm above it. Scissors set: scissors on plate, both ends over the plate, lying within 10 degrees of flat, the line from the handle end to the tips within 25 degrees of straight away from the robot (+x). Tiers (end state, highest met): 1.00 apple in bowl, towels cleared, scissors set, apple, scissors, mug, coffee and towels at rest for 1 s; 0.75 apple, towels and scissors on the plate but not set or not at rest; 0.50 apple and towels; 0.25 apple only; else 0. Cap 0.50 (any moment): any point of the scissors, while their lowest point is more than 15 mm above the table, within 72.5 mm horizontally of the cup's axis (cup radius + 30 mm, at any height); or the scissors falling faster than 0.8 m/s. Permanent zero (any moment, cannot be undone): mug tilted more than 8 degrees, the cup's axis moved more than 15 mm from where it stood at the start, or the coffee more than 12 mm off the cup's axis or 20 mm above where it started (coffee spilt); scissors off the table. Every threshold is a development estimate pending calibration. The trial ends at the run limit or once 1.00 has held for 1 s.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only. Paper towels are rigid thin plates (no bending or crumpling); coffee is a rigid cylinder standing in the mug, and spilling is proxied by the mug's tilt and displacement and by the cylinder leaving the cup; the apple is a sphere because library models can only rest on the table, not on the towels. The scissors are one rigid closed body (the blades do not open). Which arm handles which object, and where the scissors are held, are not scored.
